story_type: racing sailboat capsized far offshore, five in a life raft, beacon, helicopter basket hoist
hook: Their sailboat capsized 197 miles out. Five people, one raft.
narration: Five sailors were in a life raft, one hundred ninety seven miles off San Diego.
Their forty foot sailboat, the Crosswave, had capsized during a race to Cabo San Lucas.
Their emergency beacon sent its position by satellite, which is how a helicopter finds a raft this small.
A Coast Guard Jayhawk flew out from San Diego, and its rescue swimmer went into the water beside the raft.
Then the basket brought them up, one at a time.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted all five out of the raft and flew them back to San Diego.
title: Capsized 197 miles out, five in a raft
description:
On Oct. 28, 2009, a Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk crew from Sector San Diego hoisted five people from a life raft after their 40-foot sailboat Crosswave capsized 197 miles southwest of San Diego during the Baja Ha-Ha race.

extra_sources.excerpt: SAN DIEGO - An MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Coast Guard Sector San Diego rescued five people after their sail boat capsized 197 miles southwest of San Diego, Wednesday morning. The Coast Guard received a distress signal from a 406-MHz Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon registered to the Crosswave, a 40 foot sail boat participating in the Baja Ha Ha race, shortly after 10 a.m. A helicopter was launched from Sector San Diego, and a C-130 from Air Station Sacramento provided long range coverage. Once on scene, the helicopter crew found the five people in a life raft, and subsequently hoisted them into the helicopter. One of the rescued individuals had a minor hand injury. All five people were transported to Sector San Diego. The Baha Ha Ha is sailboat race from San Diego to Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, that began Monday.
